records.subagent_summary: All 8 rollouts (execution 149.138) scored 0: despite the incumbent's ban on global case splits, every rollout still opened separate 'sum' and 'product' cases, and inside the sum case argued that a holder of v immediately knows 2002-v, which credits the speaker with knowing the public number's role; four then declared the puzzle contradictory and boxed an arbitrary factor (143, 154, 13) while three burned the 16k cap looping. The revision replaces abstract 'recount jointly' language with two concrete steps the failures skipped: evaluate each statement strictly from that speaker's own view using only facts they were told, and replay every statement against any surviving scenario before answering, with an explicit widen-the-unstated-features rule instead of guessing when nothing survives.

All 8 round-7 rollouts scored 1, so training is saturated and the signal is token waste and transfer: the shortest, cleanest rollout (3.7k tokens, 6 hedges) ignored the incumbent's diameter-endpoints shortcut entirely and went straight to z=x+iy, square, divide by the x^2+y^2 coefficient, complete the square, while the four longest (5.1k-12.2k tokens, up to 37 hedges) all entered the endpoint/midpoint route early and only reached the coordinate route much later. The 12.2k outlier then stalled on two self-inflicted crises the endpoint route creates: a negative-looking radius from a negative 1-k^2 denominator (10 'negative' mentions) and applying the 1/n root while nth powers still stood. The revision therefore inverts the priority to make the coordinate route primary, explicitly drops the endpoint shortcut, and adds a portable rule that lengths are magnitudes so a negative expression is a sign of the divisor, not an error.

This round scored 5/8; all three failures collapsed the same way, asserting from extent alone that the 1x1 shape lies wholly inside the 2x2 one (one committed 4 outright, two burned the 16384-token cap oscillating between that containment claim and unsuccessful tangency/distance-to-side searches). The incumbent already forbids the containment claim but gives no checkable reason, so the student overrides the ban with a size argument. This revision supplies the mechanism: a corner covers only the intersection of two half-planes whose boundary lines run through S's interior, so some of S is necessarily outside, which makes extent-based containment self-refuting and keeps the rotation-partition proof that earned the best held-out score.

My 8 public rollouts with the incumbent scored 5/8 and, unlike round 5, all three failures were token-cap truncations rather than wrong answers, so the fix must target looping, not aggregation. Two of the three re-imposed a constant step inside a single function's own values, concluded 'each function contributes at most one term', hit the contradiction with the hint's product, and oscillated until truncation; the third had already accepted the product and begun a clean final write-up but restarted the exposition and ran out of space. The revision therefore adds the one missing fact that kills the loop (a function's index group need not be consecutive, so its own successive differences carry no information) and a terminate-once-settled rule, trimming the verbose construction clause to stay under the token cap.

All 8 public rollouts were correct (train_i=1.0), so train is saturated and transfer binds. The two most expensive rollouts (13360 and 10264 tokens) each spent hundreds of lines restating the single vector equality as equal diagonal midpoints or vertex sums; one of them derived a y-gap of 3 instead of 1 from that restatement and then wrote six passages about the problem being contradictory before recovering, while every clean short rollout took the displacement directly off the vector and never mentioned midpoints. Prior-round failures on this question had the same shape plus assigning a translated vertex a y from the carried shift rather than from f, so this revision replaces the base-under-1 warning with a one-line base flip that removes the direction trap outright, names the redundant-midpoint detour as the thing to skip, and keeps only the reduction lever, root filter, and evaluate-f rule.

This round scored 2/8; both successes converted the asked position into a requirement on which move happens last, then multiplied 1/2 only over the genuinely free binary steps, while five of the six failures used a uniformity shortcut (1/4 from 'each bag equally likely per position', 1/2, or 1/16 from 1/2^n) and one still claimed the order is forced. Rounds 1-6 show every rewrite longer than the 83-token incumbent lost held-out monotonically, so this proposal is deliberately near incumbent length and keeps only the one mechanism the successful rollouts used plus the orientation rule.

All 8 rollouts scored 0 (7 hit the 16384-token cap) with the same failure seen every round: each set P(x)=sum a_i x^i and reread condition k as P(k)=0, swapping the node with the condition exponent, then spent the budget on the resulting phantom free root and reported 1/2005, 0, 1/4008, -1/2004, or a harmonic sum. Six prior proposals at 132-184 tokens all lost heldout accuracy relative to the 82-token incumbent, roughly monotonically in length, so this round tests the untried short region: keep the incumbent's proven functional register and add only the one missing operational move, a combination of the given conditions forming a test polynomial that isolates a single weight.

6/8 public rollouts were correct and both failures shared one mode: they never mentioned gcd or maximality at all, instead lifting the stated group count directly as the unit count, dividing every listed total by it, finding each quotient whole, and treating that as confirmation. Rounds 5 and 6 attacked this by expanding the gcd machinery (front-loaded warning, maximality certificate) and both raised train while collapsing heldout from 0.2125 to 0.1125 and 0.0625, so more narrow divisibility apparatus demonstrably hurts transfer. Since lambda=5 I instead replaced the incumbent's near-vacuous grouping clause with a broadly portable quantity-labelling discipline - state in words what each given number counts before using it, and confirm you reported the quantity asked - which blocks the observed substitution without adding item-specific gcd steps.

All 8 public rollouts were correct again (8/8, 3.5k-5.7k tokens, none truncated), so the training question is saturated under the incumbent and every remaining point is transfer. Reading them, the centered ansatz and the factored both-branch condition are picked up verbatim and cause no trouble, but the incumbent's data step is stated only as a fact about this problem's two values ('their sum pins r, their difference pins A'), so rollouts treat it as a lookup rather than a method and several detour into re-solving the pair one equation at a time. This revision keeps the proven trigger, centered ansatz, branch derivation, and verification spine byte-identical and rewrites only that step as the portable rule that constraints differing in the sign of one part should be added and subtracted to decouple the unknowns, which should carry to unseen problems whose given data is not p(0),q(0).

Only 2/8 correct; six failures shared two root causes. Several rollouts spent thousands of tokens unsure whether one application is the whole loop over k or a single block swap, then counted sub-steps as applications (one reported 3 for the 4-letter size, another invented a k=n sub-step that does not exist), and the rest collapsed a length-L block swap into one transposition and asserted order 2 untraced. Two length-capped rollouts had a small-size count that contradicted their own larger-size counts and concluded no single formula exists instead of redoing the cheap small case, so the revision defines the application boundary up front, guards the sub-step range, and tells the student to distrust the small case rather than go piecewise.
